title: Loneliness and Social Isolation Can Rob Men of Six Disease-Free Years of Their Lives - Nautilus
gist: A Nature Communications study links social disconnectedness to poorer health with age, with the headline finding that loneliness and social isolation can cost men six disease-free years; the captured text mainly distinguishes objective isolation from subjective loneliness.

insights.claim: Loneliness and social isolation can rob men of six disease-free years of life, according to a new study in Nature Communications.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Quantifies social health as a healthspan factor, relevant to aging-economy and insurance models.
insights.locator: Loneliness and Social Isolation Can Rob Men

insights.claim: Social isolation is an objective count of social contacts, while loneliness is a subjective feeling; one can be lonely without being isolated and vice versa.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Interventions and products must target perception as well as contact counts.
insights.quote: Social isolation is an objective measure of how many social contacts like friends and family you have. Loneliness, on the other hand, is a subjective account of your feelings.
